description: The one source of category ids, their hierarchy and the semantic element contracts. Admin, resolver, admission and the author context read this file; nothing restates these lists.

parts.seat: `.seat[data-ph="N"]` — a numbered seat for what the page cannot draw (an image, a 3D model); variants `.seat.avatar` `.seat.portrait` `.seat.logo` `.seat.back` `.seat.icon`. A seat is a placement, not a material.

foundation.structure:

`. `.body` is a 12-column x 6-row grid; each body child states only `style="grid-column:A / span N; grid-row:B / span M"`. `.group` (a row of equal members; `.group.col` `.group.two` `.group.three`), `.stack` (a column), `.split` (two columns, first narrower; `.split.wide-left` reverses) hold several members of one slot. A cover is `class="slide cover"`: no head/body; `.page` holds a `.lockup` (`.kicker` + `.title` + `.lead`) placed with `.at-center` `.at-left` `.at-bottom-left` `.at-top-left`, an optional `.meta` line, and optional `.deco` (the foundation's cover graphic) or `.seat.back`.

contracts.structure: `.card` > `.parts` — variants `.on` (emphasis: accent fill) `.quiet` `.line` (outlined) `.tone-1…5`. Text parts inside `.parts`: `.kick` (small line above) `.fig` (the figure; `<small>` for its unit) `.name` `.note` `.mark` (icon or number).
`.pill` > `.parts` — a one-line capsule (mark + name + note); variants `.on` `.quiet` `.line`.

`.callout` — one sentence that concludes the page, written as `

문장 핵심 구절

`, optional `.icon` before it.
`.tag` — a small label inside a part; `.hl` — a highlight inside running text.

`.list` > `.item` (`.name` + `.note`) — the element draws each item's marker: a dot, a tick on `.list.check`, the item's number on `.list.num`; `.list.divided` rules the items apart. Never write numbers into the items. An item's own `.mark` holds only an icon.
`.quote` > `<blockquote>` + `.by` (`.seat.avatar` + `.name` + `.note`) — variant `.quote.big`.

`.headline` > `.kick` (optional small line above) + `<h2>` (the heading; `<b>` on the words that carry it) + `.note` (optional one-line subhead) — a heading set inside the body, apart from the page head; variants `.headline.big` (a statement-size heading that is the page's point), `.headline.center`, `.headline.on` (on the accent ground).

`.prose` > `

` × 1–4 (running text; `` for emphasis) — body copy set as paragraphs; variants `.prose.lead` (a larger opening paragraph), `.prose.cols` (paragraphs flow into two columns), `.prose.quiet` (secondary text).
`.stat` > `.parts` (`.fig` + `.name` + `.note`) — a bare figure without a surface; `.stats` > `.stat` × n a row of them with dividers.
`.delta` — `12.1억15.6억` before → after; the arrow is drawn by the element.
`.bars` `style="--max:N"` > `.bar` `style="--v:N"` (`<b>` value + `<span>` label; `.bar.on`, `.bar.tone-N`) — vertical bars; `.bars.h` horizontal.
`.lines` `style="--max:N"` > `.pt` `style="--v:N"` (`<b>` + `<span>`) — a line over equal steps, drawn by the element from the points.
`.donut` `style="--v:N"` (0–100) > `.fig` + `.name` — one share of a whole; `.donuts` > `.donut` × n a row of them.
`.meter` `style="--v:N"` (0–100) > `.name` + `.fig` — a horizontal progress bar; several stack in a `.stack`.
`.tablebox` > `<table class="table">` with explicit `<thead>`/`<tbody>`; `.pick` on the cells of the column that is the point; `.num` on numeric cells.
`.legend` > `.key.tone-N` — a chart legend.
`.steps` > `.step` (`.mark` number + `.name` + `.note`) — joined left to right by the element's connector; `.steps.col` downward.
`.track` > `.stop` (`.kick` date + `.name` + `.note`; `.stop.on`) — points on a line; `.track.alt` alternates above/below; `.track.col` runs downward.
`.cycle` > `.core` + `.node` × 3–6 — members around a centre, arrows drawn by the element.
`.hub` > `.core` + `.spoke` × 3–6 (`.mark` + `.name` + `.note`) — a centre with members on spokes.
`.funnel` > `.stage` × 3–6 (`.name` + `.fig`), each `style="--v:N"` (0–100) for its width.
`.pyramid` > `.level` × 3–5 (`.name` + `.note`).

`.matrix` > `.axis-x` (2 labels) `.axis-y` (2 labels) + `.cell` × 4 (`.cell.on`) — a 2×2 — variant `.matrix.swot`: no axes; the four cells are Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats in that order, each with `.kick` (S/W/O/T) + `.name` + `.list`.
`.venn` > `.set` × 2–3 (`.name`; `.set.on`) + optional `.core`.
`.org` > `.root` + `.branch` × 2–4 (`.node` + `.leaf` …) — a tree; connectors drawn by the element.
`.flowchart` > `.node` (`.start` `.ask` `.end`) placed with `style="grid-column; grid-row"` and connector classes `to-r to-d to-l to-u` — connectors and arrowheads drawn by the element.
`.arch` > `.layer` × 2–5 (`.name` + `.chip` …) — stacked architecture layers.
`.versus` > `.side` × 2 (+ `.side.on`) each `.name` + `.list`, with a `<b class="vs">` mark between.
`.plan` > `.name` + `.price` (`.fig` + `<small>`) + `.list.check` (+ `.tag`; `.plan.on`) — `.plans` > `.plan` × n a row.
`.person` > `.seat.avatar|.seat.portrait` + `.name` + `.note` (+ `.list`) — `.people` > `.person` × n a row.
`.logos` > `.seat.logo` × n.
`.frame` > `.seat[data-ph]` — the element's picture frame around one seat.
`.agenda` > `.entry` (`.mark` number + `.name` + `.note`; `.entry.on`) — the contents list.

`.stacks` `style="--max:N"` > `.sbar` × 2–12 (`<span>` label + `.seg` × 2–5, each `style="--v:N"` with `<b>` value and `.tone-N`; `.sbar.on`) — segments stacked in order; `.stacks.pct` 100% bars (each bar's segments sum to 100, --max unused); `.stacks.h` horizontal. Pair with a `.legend` for the segment names.

`.waterfall` `style="--max:N"` > `.move` × 3–10 (`<b>` value + `<span>` label), each `style="--from:A; --to:B"` (the running total before and after this step) and one of `.up` `.down` `.total` (a total bar stands from 0 to --to) — the element draws floating bars and the connectors between consecutive steps.

`.areas` `style="--max:N"` > `.series` × 1–4 (`.tone-N`; `.name`) > `.pt` × 3–12 `style="--v:N"` (`<b>` value optional) + `.axis` > `<span>` × the point count (labels) — filled areas over equal steps, drawn by the element the way it draws a line; `.areas.stacked` stacks the series: on it each point's --v is the running total up to and including its series, series listed bottom first.

`.scatter` `style="--xmax:N; --ymax:M"` > `.axis-x` (`<span>` name) + `.axis-y` (`<span>` name) + `.dot` × 3–24 `style="--x:A; --y:B"` (`<span>` label optional; `.dot.on`, `.dot.tone-N`) — points on two value axes from 0; `.scatter.bubble` sizes each dot by its `--r` (0–100).

`.spark` `style="--max:N"` > `<span>` × 5–24 each `style="--v:N"` — a mini trend with no axes or labels, set inline beside a figure: nests inside a `.stat` or `.card` `.parts` (after `.fig`) or stands alone in a small cell; `.spark.bars` mini bars; `.spark.up` / `.spark.down` colours the trend as good or bad.

`.heat` `style="--cols:N"` > `.heads` (`<span>` × N column labels) + `.row` × 2–12 (`.name` + `.cell` × N each `style="--v:N"` 0–100, `<b>` value optional) — density by colour strength; `.heat.calendar` square day cells with no row names (rows are weekdays, `.heads` the weeks).

`.waffle` > `.units` > `<span class="u">` × 10–100 (`.u.on` the counted share, `.u.tone-N` a second share) + `.fig` + `.name` — a share as counted units, '10명 중 3명'; `.waffle.figures` draws each unit as a person pictogram. Several stand side by side in a `.group`.

`.treemap` > `.branch` × 1–5 `style="--v:N"` (its share of the whole, 0–100; `.name`) > `.tile` × 1–8 `style="--v:N"` (its share of the branch, 0–100; `.name` + `.fig`; `.tile.on`) — nested rectangles whose areas follow the shares; with one branch the tiles fill the whole.

`.sankey` > `.source` (`.name` + `.fig`) + `.branch` × 2–6 `style="--v:N"` (share of the source, 0–100; `.name` + `.fig`; `.branch.on` the main path, `.branch.out` a drop-off) — bands as thick as their share flow from the source to each branch; a `.branch` may itself hold `.branch` × 2–4 for a second split.

`.radar` `style="--max:N; --n:K"` (K = 3–8 axes) > `.axis` × K (`.name`) + `.series` × 1–3 (`.tone-N`; `.name`) `style="--v1:A; --v2:B; …; --vK:Z"` — each series a filled polygon over K spokes, first axis at the top, clockwise.

`.bullet` `style="--v:N; --target:T"` (0–100; optional `--low:L; --high:H` qualitative bands) > `.name` + `.fig` (+ `.note` for the target) — actual against target and bands in one row; `.bullets` > `.bullet` × n stacks them.

`.slope` `style="--max:N"` > `.heads` (`<span>` before + `<span>` after) + `.pair` × 2–8 `style="--a:A; --b:B"` (`.name` + `<b class="a">` + `<b class="b">`; `.pair.on`) — each item's change between two moments; `.slope.dumbbell` draws horizontal dumbbells instead of slope lines.

`.roadmap` `style="--cols:N"` > `.heads` (`<span>` × N periods) + `.lane` × 2–6 (`.name` + `.bar` × 1–4 `style="--from:A; --to:B"` in periods, 0-based start and exclusive end, each `<span>` label, `.bar.on` `.bar.tone-N`; optional `.mile` `style="--at:A"` with `<span>` — a milestone point) — durations on tracks; a timeline marks moments, a roadmap spans periods.

`.swimlane` `style="--cols:N"` > `.lane` × 2–5 `style="grid-row:L"` (`.name` — the owner) + `.node` (`.start` `.ask` `.end`) placed with `style="grid-column:C; grid-row:L"` in its lane and connector classes `to-r to-d to-l to-u` — a flowchart whose rows are owners; connectors and arrowheads drawn by the element.
`.orbit` > `.ring` × 2–4, outermost first (`.name` + `.fig`, `.note` optional; `.ring.on`) — each set contains the next, e.g. TAM ⊃ SAM ⊃ SOM; inclusion, not overlap (that is a venn).

`.journey` > `.stage` × 3–7 `style="--mood:M; --next:X"` (0–100, 100 delighted; --next is the following stage's mood, omitted on the last) (`.name` + `.note` the touchpoint + `.pain` optional pain point; `.stage.on`) — stages in a row with the emotion curve drawn across them by the element.

`.mindmap` > `.core` (`.name`) + `.branch` × 2–6 (`.name` + `.leaf` × 0–4; `.branch.on`) — branches radiate left and right of the centre with curved links drawn by the element; freer than a hierarchy.

`.dtree` > `.q` (`.name` — the question) + `.opts` > `.opt` × 2–3 (`.cond` the answer on the branch + either a nested `.q` + `.opts` or an `.end` outcome with `.name`; `.end.on` the recommended outcome) — at most three questions deep; branches drawn by the element.

`.balance` `style="--tilt:T"` (−100…100, negative = the left pan weighs more) > `.pan` × 2 (`.name` + `.item` × 1–4 each `.name`; `.pan.on`) + `.fulcrum` (`<span>` verdict, optional) — two sides weighed on a beam the element tilts by --tilt.
`.grid9` > `.axis-x` (3 labels, low → high) + `.axis-y` (3 labels, low → high) + `.cell` × 9 row by row from the top (`.name` + `.note`; `.cell.on`, `.cell.tone-N`) — a nine-box such as GE-McKinsey.

`.posmap` > `.axis-x` (2 labels: low, high) + `.axis-y` (2 labels: low, high) + `.mark` × 2–12 `style="--x:A; --y:B"` (0–100; `.seat.logo` or `.name`; `.mark.on` ours) — competitors placed on two axes crossing at the centre.

`.network` > `.node` × 3–12 `style="--x:A; --y:B"` (0–100 of the box; `.name`; `.node.on`, `.node.tone-N`) + `.link` × 2–20 `style="--x1:A; --y1:B; --x2:C; --y2:D"` (its two nodes' positions; `.link.strong`) — many-to-many relations; the element draws each link as a line between its points.

`.code` > `.name` (optional file name) + `.lines` > `

` × 1–24 (one source line each, leading spaces kept; tokens wrapped as `` keyword, `` string, `` comment, `` number) — monospaced source; `.code.numbered` draws line numbers.

layout.structure: A slide layout: a head and named slots placed on the 12 x 6 body grid, or a cover.

background.structure: One SVG on the slide's 1280x720 coordinates (viewBox `0 0 1280 720`) drawn behind the page; every fill, stroke and stop-color is `none`, a `url(#id)` it defines or a colour token `var(--name)`. A frame (`background.frame`) is the same on every page and states its inset {top,right,bottom,left}: the content box the page's margins start inside. A vector (`background.vector`) is re-drawn for each page outside the page's measured keep-out.
